I sought veterinary care for my dog ​​because I needed to renew the prescription for her continuous and controlled medication, as recommended by the veterinarian who treats her in our city. I found the clinic through the Petlove network and, when scheduling the appointment, I explained the reason for the consultation and the medication used, and no objections were raised. However, during the appointment, it became clear that the veterinarian who saw us has objections to the use of the medication, preferring alternative therapies – which is her right, in fact, but this could have been communicated at the time of scheduling. I presented all the history and documentation proving the use of the medication, and I was open to following her recommendations for the future of the treatment. I also communicated the need to continue the treatment at this time, following the veterinarian's recommendation that, in case of interruption of the medication, this should be done gradually, as there are serious risks if interrupted abruptly. The professional refused to prescribe the medication, not even prescribing a weaning process. She recommended alternative therapies, requested further consultations, and offered no consideration for any risks associated with the use of the medication in question. She repeatedly referred to the muzzle I was using – my responsibility as the owner, for her own safety – as a "gag," even though I use top-quality equipment. Throughout the consultation, I felt that my accounts were met with distrust and judgment, and that the particularities of my dog ​​mattered little; the prescription would be the same: integrative therapies. This account is to prevent other owners from falling into the same situation.
